rites.name: Kalulaneno
rites.text: Kalulaneno is the concept of the first root-tone of Morarneld, the sound that condensed the world's foundations during the Singing. It is remembered as a low, patient hum that held the early soil together long before any living thing had a voice.

rites.name: Khouktun
rites.text: Khouktun is the concept of a binding oath sworn before the Courts of Morarneld, the rule that a promise made at a trial becomes a stone the speaker must carry. In the age of the doors it was the cord that tied each council's verdict to the threshold it guarded. Its bearers are rarely powerful, but few can break what Khouktun has sealed.

rites.name: Amollus
rites.text: Amollus is a concept of Morarneld, an idea born in the Fall and the Sundering, when the worlds broke into Shards and the Pact was sworn beneath the temple flames of the Holy Age. It names the grounded discipline by which the Orders bound their vows to ash and stone.

rites.name: Halare
rites.text: Halare is a concept of the Walled Age in Morarneld, a period of holding walls, sworn orders, and the first tentative crossings between districts. Its doctrine held that flame was the measure of faith, and temples kept the hearths that were thought to bind the walls together. Its adherents taught that a well-lit wall would never fall.

rites.name: Thorath
rites.text: Thorath is the name given to the stone-hewn ward-engine that the orders of Morarneld raised during the Walled Age to keep the holding walls standing through winter sieges. It was built to bind the masonry of the great gates rather than to strike, and its makers recorded its strength in the tallies of the Holy Age temples.

rites.name: Venemiel
rites.text: Venemiel is a concept in Morarneld's Three Futures, the branching moment when the ending splits and the Library shelves each outcome as its own volume. It exists as a quiet hinge in the record, a question held open until a reader decides which shelf it belongs on.
